summary: No-ship: the proposed scope and exact-one models contradict the repository’s current execution and update topology. As designed, they introduce false-green app validation, reject intentional enforcement mirrors, and fail to detect the named pg-tools drift.
triage: review-gate SKILL.md rules govern: render EVERY finding as a full table row, the human decides each row (accept/reject/defer/question — free text), echo back before applying, max 2 rounds, append decisions.md and COMMIT it with this artifact.

findings.title: The `apps` scope hides the invalid state it must detect
findings.body: `listUnits('apps')` requires `values.yaml` before returning an app, yet the design later migrates `check-app-deploy` to this scope. An app deployment directory missing `values.yaml` will therefore disappear from the checker instead of failing its required-artifact contract. The same abstraction cannot close `check-app-netpol` vacuity: a floor over app directories can pass while its downstream NetworkPolicy selection remains zero. This introduces a deployment-breaking false green and invalidates the claimed scan-floor benefit.
findings.recommendation: Discover app units independently of required artifacts, such as from tracked `apps/*/deploy/prod` directories or another authoritative binding. Keep non-vacuity checks after each consumer’s semantic filtering, using conditional domain invariants where zero is legitimate.

findings.title: Execution venues are not a mutually exclusive ownership dimension
findings.body: The listed venue sources intentionally overlap. For example, `check-skeleton.sh` runs from both `make verify` and the required `ci.yaml` gate, while aliases such as `bun run verify:ledger` require transitive resolution to reach the underlying guard. Bats tests also execute guard scripts. Raw counting therefore reports 2+ for legitimate mirrors or 0 for unresolved aliases. Even the claimed orphan `check-credential-expiry.sh` is directly invoked by its scheduled workflow. Implementing exact-one over these venues would either fail permanently or pressure removal of useful required/local coverage.
findings.recommendation: Separate one authoritative enforcement owner from any number of wrappers, mirrors, and test invocations. Resolve command aliases transitively and require at least one authoritative reachable path; apply exact-one only to a genuinely mutually exclusive classification.

findings.title: G2’s exact-one calculation cannot detect its motivating pg-tools skew
findings.body: Under the stated calculation, Renovate path matching and `repin-pgtools.ts::CONSUMERS` are independent owners. The repository’s Renovate Kubernetes manager covers platform YAML, so current pg-tools references in `CONSUMERS` match both mechanisms and become invalid double-owners. The two omitted pg-tools consumers still match Renovate and therefore pass with exactly one owner—the opposite of the claimed D-1 detection. The model confuses generic updater reachability with the authoritative event-driven synchronizer.
findings.recommendation: Define artifact-specific owner precedence or exclusions. For pg-tools, make the repin synchronizer authoritative and separately require every matching repository reference to appear in `CONSUMERS`; treat Renovate coverage as a different freshness channel rather than a second ownership match.

next_steps: Redefine scope membership and semantic scan-floor responsibilities before implementation.
Replace G1 raw venue counting with an authoritative-owner plus reachability model.
Specify G2 ownership precedence and prove it against the current pg-tools reference set.
